diagnosis: The single biggest, clearest failure is OVER-QUANT on the three pull-open articulated tasks: OpenDoubleDoor (HARMFUL, 98%), OpenDrawer (HARMFUL, 97%), OpenSingleDoor (HARMFUL, 94%) all get compressed at near-ceiling rates with no protection, costing measured success (e.g. OpenDrawer K2/gate 0.44 vs raw 0.72). The current NO clause only covers grasping and insertion, so the gripper-on-handle pull-open phase reads as 'transporting through free space' and is compressed.
change: Extend the NO clause with ONE physical cue: when the gripper is engaged on a handle/knob and pulling a hinged door or sliding drawer open toward the robot, the arm is moving under load along a fixed hinge/slide path — constrained contact, lean NO. I phrase it as pulling-open-toward-the-robot specifically so it will NOT regress the SAFE close tasks (CloseDrawer 96%, CloseSingleDoor 96%), which are pushing a panel away and stay YES; PnP and turn tasks are untouched because no door/drawer is being pulled.
predicted_effect: Gate quant% on the three pull-open tasks should drop substantially and their gate success should recover toward raw; close-door/drawer tasks, PnP, and turn tasks should keep their current quant% and success (the cue only fires on handle-engaged pulling-open, which they do not exhibit).

diagnosis: The single clearest failure is OpenSingleDoor: HARMFUL, gate 0.68 vs raw 0.80 (-0.12 gap) with quant 57% — OVER-QUANT with no protection, even though the guidance already has a 'pulling a hinged door open toward the robot = NO' clause. Its sibling open-under-load tasks already register the cue (OpenDoubleDoor 46%, OpenDrawer 47%), so the clause is firing for those but leaking for a single swinging door, which the gate reads as a free-space 'broad sweep' rather than a constrained pull. The PnP and Turn/Coffee regressions sit at the visual ceiling or at near-zero quant (CoffeeServeMug 5%, TurnOffSinkFaucet 8%) where guidance can't move them, so they are not the target.
change: Append the VISUAL SIGNATURE of a single door opening to the existing NO door-clause — a widening gap and the door edge/handle sweeping toward the camera — so the gate recognizes a lone swinging door as the same under-load pull it already protects on double doors/drawers. This will not regress the SAFE close-doors because it keeps the direction discriminator crisp (gap WIDENING + edge toward camera = NO; gap NARROWING + panel receding = YES), which is exactly the signal that keeps CloseSingleDoor (99%) and CloseDoubleDoor (99%) compressing.
predicted_effect: OpenSingleDoor quant should fall from 57% toward the ~45% band of OpenDoubleDoor/OpenDrawer and gate success recover toward raw (~0.80). OpenDoubleDoor and OpenDrawer already trigger the clause and stay protected; CloseSingleDoor/CloseDoubleDoor keep their high quant because the cue is gated on the gap WIDENING and the edge moving toward the camera, not on door identity; all PnP/Turn tasks are untouched.

diagnosis: The single largest clear miss is a cluster of SAFE in-place rotation tasks pinned at near-zero quant: TurnOffMicrowave (0% quant, SAFE), TurnOnMicrowave (0%, SAFE), TurnSinkSpout (0%, SAFE), plus TurnOnStove/TurnOffStove low — all UNDER-QUANT. The current NO clause names 'handle OR knob' engaged in opening, so the gate over-generalizes and protects every gripper-on-knob/faucet moment, even though rotating a knob/faucet in place is measured SAFE. This is a guidance-caused over-protection distinct from the genuine door/drawer-open protection.
change: Narrow the NO clause: restrict the 'handle' word (drop 'knob') and add ONE cue stating the under-load protection applies only when a WHOLE hinged door or sliding drawer translates open, whereas rotating a knob/dial/lever/faucet handle IN PLACE (a small part spins/flips, no panel translates, nothing swings open) is light unconstrained motion → lean YES. This will not regress the door/drawer protections (Open* tasks involve a panel translating along a hinge/slide, which the cue explicitly still protects) and touches no PnP/grasp/insert behaviour.
predicted_effect: The in-place rotation tasks (TurnOffMicrowave, TurnOnMicrowave, TurnSinkSpout, TurnOnSinkFaucet, Turn*Stove) should move off 0%/low quant toward compressing, recovering their SAFE speedup, with success retained since the data labels them SAFE. Door/drawer opens (OpenDrawer, OpenSingleDoor, OpenDoubleDoor) and all grasp/insert/PnP tasks stay put because the protected motion — a panel translating under load — is unchanged.

diagnosis: The single clearest guidance-attributable failure is CloseDoubleDoor: it is labeled HARMFUL yet the gate quantizes it 100% (gate 0.66, raw 0.86) because the guidance treats every closing motion as unconstrained 'panel moving away → YES'. The sibling closing tasks CloseSingleDoor (SAFE, 100%) and CloseDrawer (SAFE, 80%) are correctly compressing, so the problem is specifically the double-leaf case, not closing in general. (PnPCounterToCab's 0.50→0.00 and OpenDoubleDoor's 0.94→0.76 are larger numerically but both sit at already-correct quant levels — collapse despite low/no over-quant — so they read as run instability, not a separable visual cue.)
change: Add ONE physical exception inside the existing 'closing → YES' clause: when the closing motion brings two SEPARATE door leaves toward each other to meet and align at a central vertical seam, the final approach is a precise two-edge mating (like seating one panel against the other) → lean NO near closure. This is visually distinctive (two converging leaves + center seam) and cannot fire on a single leaf or a drawer face, which have no mating seam — so CloseSingleDoor and CloseDrawer keep compressing, and OpenDoubleDoor (gap widening, not meeting) is untouched.
predicted_effect: CloseDoubleDoor gate quant% drops from 100% (protecting the delicate two-leaf alignment near closure) and its success recovers toward raw (~0.86). CloseSingleDoor, CloseDrawer, and all open-door tasks stay put because the cue requires two converging leaves meeting at a center seam. Note that PnPCounterToCab and OpenDoubleDoor are not addressed this cycle (suspected instability, not a visual-cue issue).
